title: Phenol Chloroform DNA Extraction Optimized for HMW gDNA from Coccidioides spp.
author: Mitchell Bryant
materials: Move all supplies into hood to begin extraction. Before scraping plates, take 25:24:1 phenol:chloro:isoamyl tubes out of the –20 degree freezer (or 4C) in order to defrost. Chloroform and alcohol can be left in freezer- works better if cold.
minutes. Be sure to mix well via inversion.

steps.title: Prepare Lysis Buffer
steps.instruction: Prepare the lysis buffer in a sterile 50 ml falcon tube within a hood using the following components:

substeps.instruction: Combine 30 ml Mol. Biol grade water, 5 ml 3M NaOAc (pH 6.0), 2.5 ml 10% SDS, 10 ml 0.5 M EDTA (pH 8.0), and 2.5 ml 1M Tris HCl (pH 7.5) for a total volume of 50 ml.
If precipitate has formed, heat the buffer in a water bath at 65°C.
Immediately before use, add $\beta$-mercaptoethanol ($\beta$-ME) at a concentration of 10 $\mu$L per 10 mL of buffer.
Aliquot 1 ml of lysis buffer into each required bead tube (e.g., sterilized 1mm BioSpec glass beads and sterile screw cap 2 ml tubes).

steps.title: Prepare Fungal Sample
steps.instruction: Collect mycelia from plates using a sterile #10 scalpel, avoiding as much media as possible. Change scalpels between plates/strains.

substeps.instruction: Option 1 (N2/Flash Freeze): Scrape plates 1 day prior, place material in a conical tube (1 plate per 2-3 bead tubes), and flash freeze at -80°C overnight or in liquid nitrogen for 5-10 minutes immediately before extraction.
Option 2 (Direct): Add mycelia directly to the bead tube containing 1 ml lysis buffer on the day of extraction.

steps.title: Lysis and Homogenization
steps.instruction: Perform cell lysis and homogenization of the sample.

substeps.instruction: Optional: Heat kill at 80°C for 30 min to denature DNAse (required if not working in a vented BSC).

Bead beat the sample. For standard lysis, beat for 60-120 seconds at 6m/s, using 2-minute rest periods every 30 seconds to prevent overheating. If DNA shearing is a concern, perform only one 30-second cycle at 6m/s.

steps.title: RNA Removal and Clarification
steps.instruction: Remove RNA and clear the lysate.

substeps.instruction: Add 50 $\mu$L of RNAse A to each sample and incubate at 37°C.
Centrifuge the samples for two minutes at 10,000g.
Pipet off approximately 650 $\mu$L of the supernatant and transfer to a new 1.5 ml tube.

steps.title: Phenol-Chloroform Extraction
steps.instruction: Perform organic extraction to isolate DNA in a ducted cabinet.

substeps.instruction: Add an equal volume of phenol:chloroform:isoamyl (25:24:1) pH 8 to the sample (e.g., 650 $\mu$L).
Mix by inversion for ten minutes using a nutator or slow rotation; do not vortex.
Centrifuge for ten minutes at full speed (14,000g).
Carefully pipet off the top layer (approx. 600 $\mu$L), avoiding the white loose phase layer, and transfer to a new 1.5 ml tube.
If the sample is contaminated with the phase layer, repeat the phenol:chloroform:isoamyl wash (equal volume, 10 min inversion, 10 min full-speed centrifuge).
Add an equal volume of chloroform:isoamyl (24:1) to the sample (e.g., 600 $\mu$L).
Mix by inversion for two to ten minutes.
Centrifuge in a 4°C fridge for ten minutes at maximum speed.
Pipet off the top layer (approx. 500 $\mu$L), avoiding the phase layer, and transfer to a new 1.5 ml tube.

steps.title: DNA Precipitation
steps.instruction: Precipitate the DNA using cold isopropanol.

substeps.instruction: Add 2/3rds volume of cold isopropanol (e.g., 333 $\mu$L) and mix by inversion.
Incubate on ice for 10-20 minutes (or optionally at 4°C overnight, but not exceeding 12 hours to avoid salt precipitate).
Centrifuge in a 4°C fridge for ten minutes at maximum speed.

steps.title: DNA Washing and Drying
steps.instruction: Wash the DNA pellet to remove salts and solvents.

substeps.instruction: Decant isopropanol and add approximately 500 $\mu$L of cold 70% ethanol; loosen the pellet by flicking the tube.
Centrifuge in a 4°C centrifuge for five minutes at maximum speed.
Decant ethanol and add approximately 300 $\mu$L of cold 95% ethanol.
Centrifuge in a 4°C fridge for five minutes at maximum speed.
Pour off ethanol and invert tubes on a paper towel for 10-20 minutes to allow excess ethanol to evaporate.

steps.title: DNA Rehydration and Quality Control
steps.instruction: Resuspend the DNA and verify the yield.

substeps.instruction: Add nuclease-free water (or TE): 50 $\mu$L for small pellets or 200 $\mu$L for large pellets (default suggestion is 50 $\mu$L).
The following morning, flick tubes to mix and spin down for 2 seconds.
Check concentration via 1% gel: mix 2 $\mu$L DNA, 8 $\mu$L water, and 2 $\mu$L loading dye; run at 70 V for approximately 2 hours.
Quantify DNA for applications (e.g., 1-2 $\mu$g for WGS) or perform serial dilutions (1:10, 1:100, 1:1000) for PCR.
